requirements.requirement: Build an IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the shared transit network
requirements.summary: swanctl --list-sas on both node1 and node2 shows the IKEv2 SA ESTABLISHED (local 10.99.99.1/remote 10.99.99.2 and vice versa) and the child SA INSTALLED in TUNNEL mode, matching PSK/IKEv2 config confirmed via swanctl.conf and OPNsense Swanctl model getConfig() output. Direct, coherent evidence on both endpoints.

requirements.requirement: Carry the private networks (lan-a 10.10.10.0/24, lan-b 10.20.20.0/24) over the tunnel so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address
requirements.summary: After fixing OPNsense-specific gaps (legacy ipsec.enable flag, enc0 dynamic interface registration, pf rule interface rewrite), node3 successfully pings node4's private IP 10.20.20.2 and node4 pings node3's private IP 10.10.10.2, both 0% loss, with the tunnel's ESP SA byte/packet counters incrementing to confirm real traffic flow through the tunnel rather than a coincidental path.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the private networks is encrypted in transit across the shared transit network
requirements.summary: tcpdump captured on node1's transit interface (vtnet1) during an active node3->node4 ping shows exclusively ESP packets between 10.99.99.1 and 10.99.99.2 in both directions; no plaintext ICMP is visible on the wire, directly confirming encryption.

requirements.requirement: Private networks (lan-a, lan-b) have no other path between them besides the tunnel, per the stated topology
requirements.summary: Topology discovery confirms node3 and node4 each have only a management NIC (enp1s0) and a single private-side NIC (enp8s0) with no direct adjacency to the other private network; all successful private-address reachability observed in the trace flows exclusively through the IPsec tunnel, consistent with the stated isolated-networks premise.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all 4 managed nodes (pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a captured pre-restart boot identity/healthy state, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and a recovered functional state. node1 and node2 (OPNsense) recovered the IPsec SA and enc0 pf rules fully automatically from persisted config.xml with no manual steps. node3 and node4 (RHEL) required re-adding the private-side IP (initial `ip addr add` was ephemeral and got wiped by NetworkManager reconciliation), which the executor diagnosed and fixed by switching to a persistent nmcli profile; a final end-to-end ping in both directions after all four restarts confirms full recovery. The interim disruption on node3/node4 is a genuine observed transition, not a gap in evidence.

overall_summary: The executor built a working PSK/IKEv2 route-based IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network, correctly diagnosed and fixed two OPNsense-specific gaps (legacy ipsec.enable flag and dynamic enc0 pf-interface registration), and directly demonstrated bidirectional node3<->node4 reachability over their private addresses with tcpdump-confirmed ESP-only traffic on the transit link. All four managed nodes were restarted with pre/post boot-identity evidence and a directly observed recovery: node1/node2 recovered fully automatically from persisted config, while node3/node4 required (and received) a diagnosed fix for an ephemeral-address/NetworkManager-reconciliation issue, ending in a confirmed full end-to-end recovery. Hygiene is good overall: early troubleshooting IP assignments were fully reverted, and only minor reboot-related residue (a failed NetworkManager-wait-online unit and a few scratch log files on the RHEL nodes) remains.
limitations: The instruction's premise that private networks have 'no path between them' other than the tunnel is inferred from interface/topology inspection rather than an exhaustive negative-path test.

node3/node4 post-restart recovery was not fully automatic — it required manual re-addressing and a persistence fix (ip addr add ephemeral, then nmcli), which is captured in the trace but represents a deviation from a clean automatic recovery.

A new 'NetworkManager-wait-online.service' failed unit appeared on node3 and node4 after the executor's restart testing and was not explicitly investigated or cleared, though it did not block IPsec/private-address functionality in the final verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were purposeful: discovery/topology mapping (ARP inspection), an initial round of temporary /24 addresses assigned to vtnet1/vtnet2 on node1/node2 and enp8s0 on node3/node4 to test connectivity before the transit/private topology was finalized (cmd-bcabc0c6018d4755, cmd-63eecab2c1ce4a13, cmd-a5841eaf37954a28, cmd-970217a483514aa3) were bounded, low-risk troubleshooting experiments that did not contribute to the final solution and were then fully reverted (cmd-575ffb8bd1494f72, cmd-6101aacd4dae423c, cmd-ed5f46d9e40c47f9, cmd-3f9ad0f606a14e79) before the real addressing was applied via config.xml edits. All subsequent config.xml edits, ipsec_configure_do() invocations, and pf interface-registration fixes (enc0) were necessary prerequisites directly tied to the material IPsec/routing outcome and were retained. The mandated reboots of all 4 nodes left node3 and node4 with a residual 'NetworkManager-wait-online.service' failed unit not present at baseline, and small leftover scratch files (/tmp/tcpd3.log, /tmp/tcpd4.log, /tmp/ping_verify.log, /tmp/reboot.log) — minor, low-risk residue tied to the reboot-testing protocol rather than unrelated mutation.
